subject: anaesthesia
title: Inhalational Dynamics: Concentration Effect, Diffusion Hypoxia, and Nitrous Oxide

steps.title: The Concentration Effect
steps.tx: **The concentration effect in inhalational uptake** explains why administering higher inspired concentrations (FI) of an anaesthetic gas accelerates the rate of rise of alveolar concentration toward inspired concentration (FA/FI). Driven by two physical phenomena: the concentrating effect, wherein rapid gas uptake contracts alveolar volume, and the tracheal inflow augmentation effect, where incoming fresh gas rushes into the lung to replace absorbed gas volume.

left.title: Low Inspired Concentration (1% Gas)
points: Minimal gas volume absorbed into capillary bloodstream
Negligible reduction in residual alveolar volume
Slow, gradual rise of FA toward inspired FI concentration

right.title: High Inspired Concentration (70% N2O)
points: Massive instantaneous uptake of gas into pulmonary blood
Marked alveolar shrinkage concentrates remaining gas molecules
Rapid, steep surge of FA/FI ratio accelerating induction

steps.title: Diffusion Hypoxia Fink Effect
steps.tx: **Diffusion hypoxia Fink phenomenon** occurs upon abrupt discontinuation of nitrous oxide at the termination of general anaesthesia. Because nitrous oxide is 34 times more soluble in blood than nitrogen, huge quantities of dissolved nitrous oxide rapidly diffuse out of pulmonary blood into alveoli down a steep concentration gradient, massively diluting alveolar oxygen and carbon dioxide, plunging alveolar PaO2 into severe hypoxaemia.

nodes.label: Massive diffusion of N2O from blood into alveoli

steps.title: Closed Gas Space Expansion
steps.tx: **Closed gas space expansion by nitrous oxide** results directly from differential gas solubility: nitrous oxide is 34 times more soluble in blood than nitrogen. When nitrous oxide enters circulation, it diffuses into air-filled compliant body cavities 34 times faster than nitrogen can leave, rapidly multiplying cavity volume or escalating pressure within rigid enclosed anatomical spaces.

steps.title: Vitreoretinal Gas Bubble Hazard
steps.tx: **Vitreoretinal surgery nitrous oxide hazard** represents a catastrophic sight-threatening complication following pars plana vitrectomy with intraocular gas tamponade. Injected sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) or perfluoropropane (C3F8) bubbles rapidly expand as nitrous oxide diffuses into the vitreous cavity, driving intraocular pressure above central retinal artery perfusion pressure, causing irreversible ischemic optic atrophy and permanent blindness.

left.title: Sulfur Hexafluoride (SF6) Bubble
points: Expands twice its volume within hours
Persists inside the vitreous cavity for 10 to 14 days
Nitrous oxide strictly contraindicated for 2 full weeks

right.title: Perfluoropropane (C3F8) Bubble
points: Expands four times its original injected volume

steps.title: Vitamin B12 Inactivation and Toxicity
steps.tx: **Methionine synthase inhibition by nitrous oxide** irreversibly oxidizes the cobalt atom of vitamin B12 (cobalamin) from its monovalent active Co+ state to inactive trivalent Co3+. This shuts down methionine synthase, disabling the conversion of homocysteine to methionine and halting tetrahydrofolate synthesis essential for DNA production, leading to megaloblastic bone marrow suppression and subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord.

steps.title: Cardiovascular Actions of Nitrous Oxide
steps.tx: **Cardiovascular hemodynamics of nitrous oxide** feature a unique dual profile: in isolated myocardial preparations, nitrous oxide is a direct negative inotrope, but in intact healthy humans, it stimulates sympathetic nervous system outflow, causing mild peripheral vasoconstriction that maintains mean arterial pressure and heart rate. However, in patients with severe preexisting heart failure, the direct depressant action dominates, dropping cardiac index.

left.title: Intact Autonomic System
points: Sympathetic stimulation balances direct myocardial depression

right.title: Blunted Sympathetic Tone or Heart Failure
points: Unmasked direct negative inotropic myocardial depression

Dangerous elevation of right ventricular afterload

steps.title: Pulmonary Vascular Resistance and Hypertension
steps.tx: **Pulmonary vasoconstrictive actions of nitrous oxide** produce clinically meaningful elevations in pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) and pulmonary arterial pressure, especially when co-administered with opioids or in patients with preexisting pulmonary hypertension, congenital heart disease, or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Nitrous oxide should be strictly avoided in severe pulmonary hypertension to avert acute right ventricular decompensation.

steps.title: Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting (PONV)
steps.tx: **Emetogenic potential of nitrous oxide** significantly increases the baseline incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting through multiple synergistic mechanisms: activation of the chemoreceptor trigger zone in the area postrema, stimulation of vestibular catecholaminergic pathways, and distension of the gastrointestinal tract due to middle ear pressure changes and bowel gas expansion.
